rows.description: A young adult who must talk to a roommate or a parent about a hard matter thinks first of what they want, states facts and feelings, and invites the other view. Preparation reduces blame language.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A person told about a mistake feels hot shame and defends automatically. Listening first, asking for an example, and delaying the response until calmer allows learning from it.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A manager or friend delays a needed truth to be nice and lets the problem grow. Delay often harms more than the discomfort of a timely, gentle conversation.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A child says your dog died or grandma is sick without softening, unaware of the effect. Children speak truth plainly and need to learn that words land differently on different people.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A child told about a parent's job loss or a pet's death may go quiet, ask odd questions or carry on playing. Reactions are varied and delayed, and honest, simple explanations reassure better than hiding.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager conceals a failed test or a mistake for weeks out of fear of a parent's reaction. Fear of the response, not the news itself, drives concealment.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A young adult tells a friend about a painful truth, such as a breakup or a cancelled plan, in plain words, stays present and does not over-explain. Clear, short, warm delivery works better than hints.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A person told about a layoff or a diagnosis in the family goes flat and says okay. Shock often looks like calm, and the real reaction arrives hours or days later.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22
related mind states: surprise, detachment, calm

rows.description: A child asks questions and often accepts any answer. Answers that invite further wondering, such as what do you think, teach that questions lead somewhere.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A child asks many questions to keep an adult engaged, not because of the topic. Noticing the need for connection and responding to it can reduce the pressure.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 18–22, 23–26
